articles.title: Chrome
articles.summary: Smooth pale mirror surface with faint diagonal brushed striping; reflects surroundings like polished liquid metal, colour comes from what you spray. Reads as a smooth, slightly cloudy polished metal; stripes and specks melt into an even bright reflective sheen that takes your colour as a metallic tint.
articles.what: Perfect mirror reflection — M255 R2 pure chrome. The ultimate show car base. Reflects environment like liquid metal. Up close: Very fine diagonal hairline striping running one way across a smooth surface, with a few tiny pale specks and faint soft cloudy shading underneath. The stripes are only a few pixels wide and barely raised in tone; the surface is calm, not rough. From a distance: Reads as a smooth, slightly cloudy polished metal; stripes and specks melt into an even bright reflective sheen that takes your colour as a metallic tint. Measured spec (average): metal 226, roughness 27, coat 15. Shine: mirror. Metal: full. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: show car, gt / sports car, open wheel.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Chrome on the hood".
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and doors: wide panels show the reflections
Bumpers and trim: classic chrome placement
Keep numbers dark, bold and outlined; a reflective base can darken or wash out coloured numbers.
Bold stripes or racing livery graphics: smooth bright metal makes strong colours pop
Pairs well with: any colour tint, black, deep blue, gold.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not a perfect mirror chrome like Foundation Chrome: there is a faint diagonal brush and specks, and metal is 226 not 255
Not brushed aluminium: the grain is much finer and gloss stays high
Avoid: coloured full-metal numbers can darken, keep strong background contrast, large flat reflections that hide body shape.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 226 (true metallic), roughness 27 (wet mirror gloss), clearcoat 15 (no clearcoat).
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Metal takes on the paint colour: light and mid colours keep the sparkle, very dark colours swallow it. Avoid: coloured full-metal numbers can darken, keep strong background contrast, large flat reflections that hide body shape.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: bold stripes or racing livery graphics: smooth bright metal makes strong colours pop; fine geometric lines or fades: little texture to fight
Patterns to avoid: fine glitter or carbon weave: busy overlays clash with the brushed diagonal and the mirror look
Spec overlays that work: wave or ripple roughness: adds a liquid, reflective distortion; soft clearcoat haze: turns the mirror into satin chrome
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

It is a pure surface-sheen setting. From a distance: A uniform flat matte in whatever colour you give it; no sparkle, no texture, light just scatters softly.
